problem:
For the function $f(x)$ and $g(x)$, you're given the following data:

$$
f(4)=-3,\,{f}^{′}(4)=-1,\,g(4)=2,\,{g}^{′}(4)=\frac{1}{4}
$$

Compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)g(x))$ at $x=4.$

feedback.problem:
The values of functions $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ and their derivatives at $x=4$ are given in the table below.

| $x$ | $f(x)$ | $g(x)$ | ${f}^{′}(x)$ | ${g}^{′}(x)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $4$ | $2\pi $ | $-3$ | $\pi $ | $5$ |

Compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)g(x))$ at $x=4.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Using the product rule, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)g(x))=f(x){g}^{′}(x)+g(x){f}^{′}(x).
$$

At the point where $x=4,$ this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)g(x))|}_{x=4} & =f(4){g}^{′}(4)+g(4){f}^{′}(4) \\  & =2\pi \cdot 5+(-3)\cdot \pi  \\  & =7\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
